translations.text: The Song of Songs, which belongs to Solomon. He says:
Let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth, for your breasts are better than wine.
The fragrance of your ointments surpasses all oils. Your name is an ointment that has been blessed and poured out. That is why the young women loved you and drew you after them.

We will run after the fragrance of your ointments. The king brought me into his chamber. We will rejoice and be glad in you. We will love your breasts more than wine, for the upright one has loved you.
I am black but beautiful among the daughters of Israel, like the tents of Kedar and like the curtains of Solomon.
Do not look at me because I am black. The sun has scorched me and left me behind. My mother's sons fought against me. They made me guard the vineyards, but I did not guard my own vineyard.
Tell me, then, you whom my soul loves: where do you tend your flock, and where do you rest it at noon? Do not make me go veiled among the flocks of your companions.
If you do not know me, you who are beautiful among women, go out behind the flocks and tend your young goats among the shepherds' tents.
You who are beside me, I have compared you to my mare among Pharaoh's chariots.
Your cheeks are beautiful like turtledoves; your neck is beautiful like necklaces.
We will make a gold ornament for you with silver markings.
Until the king lay down in his place, my nard gave off its fragrance.
My brother is a bundle of myrrh to me; he will stay between my breasts.
My brother is a cluster of henna in the vineyards of En-gedi.
Look, you are beautiful, my companion! Look, you are beautiful! Your eyes are dove's eyes.
Look, you are lovely, my brother, and beautiful to look at. You cast shade over our bed.
The beams of our house are made from the trees of Lebanon; the timbers of our ceiling are cypresses.
I am the flower of the field and the lily of the valleys.
Like a lily among thorns, so is my companion among the other women.
Like an apple tree among the trees of the forest, so is my brother among the young men. I desired his shade and sat beneath it, and his fruit is sweet in my mouth.
Bring me into the house of wine; establish love for me.
Strengthen me with ointments and surround me with apples, for his love has seized me.
His left hand is beneath my head, and his right hand will embrace me.
I put you under oath, daughters of Jerusalem, by the powers and the forces of the field, to awaken my love and rouse her until she wishes.
My brother's voice reached me. Look, he has come, running over the mountains and leaping over the hills!
My brother is like a gazelle or a young deer on the mountains of Bethel. Look, he is looking from behind our wall, looking out through the windows.
And my brother spoke to me through the lattices, saying, “Get up and come, my companion, my beautiful dove.”
For look, winter has passed; the rain has moved on and gone to its place.
The flowers have appeared on the earth. The time for pruning has come. The voice of the turtledove has been heard in our land.
The fig tree has put out its unripe figs. The vines have blossomed and given off their fragrance. Get up and come, you who are beside me.
My beautiful dove, come! You, my dove, in the cleft of the rock beside the outer wall, show me your face and let me hear your voice, for your voice is sweet and your face is beautiful to me.
Catch the foxes for us, the little foxes that ruin the vineyards, for our vines are putting out blossoms.
My brother belongs to me, and I too belong to him,
the one who grazes among the lilies. Until the day comes to an end and the shadows withdraw, turn back, my brother, and be like a gazelle or a young deer on the mountains of the ravines.
On my bed at night I searched for the one my soul loved. I searched for him but did not find him. I called to him, but he did not hear me.
So I will get up and go around the city, through the marketplaces and the streets, and search for the one my soul loved. So I searched for him, but I did not find him.
The watchmen who patrol the city found me. I asked them, “Have you seen the one my soul loved?”

Then, when I had gone a little beyond them and passed out of their sight, I found the one my soul loved. I held him and did not let him go until I brought him into my mother’s house, into the room of the woman who conceived me.
I put you under oath, daughters of Jerusalem, by the powers and the strengths of the field, to awaken love and stir it up until it wishes.

Who is this coming up from the wilderness, from among [?] and [?], with the hand [?] to her [?], like a heap of incense that has been raised up, giving off fragrant smoke from myrrh and frankincense, from all the perfumer’s spices?
Look! Here is Solomon’s bed, with sixty mighty men surrounding it, from among the mighty men of Israel.
They all hold their swords and are trained for war. Each man has his sword on his thigh because of the terror that comes at night.
King Solomon made himself a seat from the wood of Lebanon.
He made its pillars of silver, and its backrest is gold. Its coverings are purple. Its interior is inlaid with stones, with love from the daughters of Jerusalem.
Come out, daughters of Zion, and see King Solomon wearing the crown with which his mother crowned him on the day of his wedding, on the day his heart rejoiced.
Look, my companion is beautiful! Look, you are beautiful! Your eyes are like those of doves, apart from your mouth. Your hair is like the herds of goats that have appeared in Gilead.
Your teeth are like flocks of shorn sheep that have come up from the water. They all have twin offspring, and none among them is childless.
Your lips are like a scarlet thread, my bride, and your speech is beautiful. Your cheeks are like a piece of pomegranate, apart from your mouth.
Your neck stands like the tower of David, built in Talpioth. A thousand shields hang on it, along with all the arrows of the mighty warriors.
Your two breasts are like two twin gazelle fawns grazing among the lilies,
until the day comes to an end and the shadows turn away.
You are entirely beautiful, my companion, and there is no blemish in you.
Come from Lebanon, my bride! Come from Lebanon! You will come and return from the beginning of faith, from the summit of Senir and Hermon, from the lions’ dens and from the leopards’ mountains.
It has taken our heart, my sister, my bride. It has taken our heart through one of your eyes and through these [?] of your neck.
For your breasts are lovelier than wine, and the scent of your clothes surpasses all perfumes.
Your lips, my bride, drip honey. Honey and milk are on your tongue, and the scent of your clothes is like the scent of Lebanon.
My sister, my bride, is like a locked garden, a locked garden, a sealed spring.
The things you have sent us are like a paradise with the fruit of flourishing trees, henna and nard.
Nard and saffron, aromatic cane and cinnamon, with all the frankincense trees, myrrh and aloes, with all the finest perfumes.
They are like a fountain of fruit and a well of living water flowing out of Lebanon.
Rise, north wind, and come, south wind! Blow into my garden so that my perfumes give off their scent.

Let my brother go up to his garden and eat the fruit of its trees. I have entered my garden, my sister, my bride. I have gathered my myrrh with my perfume. I have eaten my bread with my honey. I have drunk my wine with my milk. You too, my friends, eat! Drink and get drunk, my brothers!

I am asleep, but my heart is awake. Listen! My brother's voice as he knocks at the door: “Open to me, my sister, my companion, my perfect dove, for my head is covered with dew, and my curled hair is covered with drops.”
I have taken off my tunic for the night. How can I put it on again? I have washed my feet. How can I dirty them?
My brother reached his hand through the opening in the door, and my heart trembled for him.
I got up to open for my brother. My hands dripped myrrh, and my fingers dripped the finest myrrh. I reached out my hand to the bolt.
I opened for my brother, but my brother had left me. My soul clung to his words. I searched for him but did not find him. I called to him, but he did not listen to me.
The watchmen patrolling the city found me. They struck me and wounded me. The guards of the walls took my cloak away from me.
I put you under oath, daughters of Jerusalem, by the powers and the forces of the field: if you find my brother, what will you tell him? Tell him that I am sick with my love.
What is your brother compared with another brother, you who are beautiful among women? What kind of brother is your brother compared with another brother, that you have put us under this oath?
This is what my brother looks like: he is white and rosy, outstanding among ten thousand.
His head is like fine gold. His curled locks hang down, black as ravens.
His eyes are like doves beside flowing waters, washed in milk, sitting beside overflowing waters.
His cheeks are like bowls of perfume giving off incense. His lips are like lilies dripping the finest myrrh.
His belly is like an ivory box resting on a violet-colored sapphire stone. His hands are beautiful, skillfully fashioned like fine gold from Tarshish.
His lower legs are marble pillars firmly set on golden bases. His appearance is like Lebanon, choice as the cedars of Lebanon.
His mouth is sweet, and he is altogether desirable. This is my brother, and this is my companion, daughters of Jerusalem.
Where has my brother gone, you who are beautiful among women? Where has your brother gone, so that we may search for him with you?
My brother went down to his garden, to the bowls of fragrant spices, to feed in the gardens and gather lilies.
I belong to my brother, and my brother belongs to me, he who grazes among the lilies.
You are beautiful, my companion, like delight, lovely like Jerusalem, fearsome like armies drawn up in formation.
Let your eyes stop looking at me, for they have carried away my heart. Your hair is like the herds of goats that have appeared in Gilead.
Your teeth are like flocks of shorn sheep that have come up from the water. They all bear twins, and none among them is without offspring.
Your lips are like a scarlet thread, and your speech is lovely. The upper part of your cheek is like a slice of pomegranate, outside your mouth.
There are sixty queens and eighty concubines, and young women beyond number.

But my perfect dove is the only one. She is her mother's only one, the chosen one of the woman who bore her. The daughters saw her; therefore the queens will call her blessed, and the concubines will praise her.
Who is this who looks out like the dawn, lovely like the moon, splendid like the sun, fearsome like armies drawn up in formation?
I went down to the walnut garden to look at the produce of the stream, to see whether the vine had blossomed and whether the pomegranate tree had bloomed. There I will give you my breasts.
My soul did not understand. He placed me among the chariots of Amminadab.
Return, return, O Adullamite woman! Return, and return again, so that we may look at you. What will you come to see in the Adullamite woman, who comes like the dances of the camps?
Daughter of Amminadab, how beautiful are your steps [?] in sandals! The contours of your thighs resemble necklaces made by the hands of a craftsman.
Your navel is like a turned bowl, filled with choice wine. Your belly is like a heap of wheat surrounded by lilies.
Your two breasts are like two fawns, twins of a gazelle.
Your neck is like an ivory tower. Your eyes are like the pools of Heshbon at the gates of the daughter of a multitude. Your nose is like the tower of Lebanon, looking toward Damascus.
Your head upon you is like Carmel, and the hair of your head is like purple. A king has been placed in the passageways.
How beautiful you have become, O love! [?]
This is your stature amid delight: it has become like a palm tree.
And I said, “I will climb the palm tree and grasp its high parts.” Your breasts will be like its clusters of grapes, and the scent of your breath is like the scent of an apple.
And your palate is like good wine, going straight to my brother, sweet upon my lips and teeth.
I belong to my brother, and he will turn toward me.
Come to me, my brother. Let us go out into the countryside and stay in the villages.

Let us go out early to our vineyards to see whether the vine has blossomed, whether the henna plants have blossomed, and whether the pomegranate foliage has blossomed. There I will give you my breasts.
Our mandrakes have given off their fragrance, and all the fruit-bearing trees at our doors have new fruit beside old fruit, which I have kept for you, my brother.
Who will give you to me as my brother, nursing at my mother's breasts? If I find you outside, I will not refrain from kissing you, and they will not despise me.
I will take hold of you and bring you into my mother's house, into the chamber of the woman who conceived me. I will give you fragrant wine to drink, and wine from your pomegranate trees.
His left hand is under my head, and his right hand will embrace me.
I have put you under oath, daughters of Jerusalem, by the powers and by the strengths of the countryside, to awaken love and rouse her until she desires it.
Who is this who comes up, entirely white, boasting of her brother? I awakened you beneath the apple tree. There I will give you my breasts.
Set me like a seal on your arm, like a seal on your heart, for love is strong like death, and jealousy is fierce like the underworld. Its burning places in the heights are like flames of fire.
Much water cannot quench love, and rivers cannot drown it. If a man gave all his wealth for love, he would be utterly despised.
Our sister is little, and she has no breasts. What, then, will we do for our sister on the day when they speak about her?
If she is a wall, we will build silver battlements around her; and if she is a door, we will fit her with cedar planks.
Look, I am a wall, and my breasts are towers. In his eyes I am like one who will find peace.
Solomon had a vineyard in a place called Baal-hamon. He gave his vineyard to keepers. Each man was to bring a thousand pieces of silver for its fruit.
My vineyard is before me. The thousand pieces of silver belong to Solomon, and the two hundred belong to those who tend its fruit.
You who dwell in the gardens, your companions are listening to your voice. Let me hear it too.
Run, my brother, and be like a gazelle or a young deer on the mountains of spices.
The Song of Songs of Solomon.
